We're also celebrating a June birthday — Ethan, we see you. Read to the end.

Product Updates

What we shipped

Technology  •  May 22, 2026

The data pipeline got a major overhaul this month with the Staging Rewrite, and while most of this work happens behind the scenes, the impact will be felt across the board.

The biggest change is how files are processed. Instead of the old batch approach, files now move into raw tables as they arrive, which means daily jobs run faster and any file can be reprocessed on demand without hunting down the original source. No more locating, warming, or decrypting just to fix a problem.

The rewrite also brought stronger deduplication, cleaner date and number handling, and broader automated testing — all of which means better data quality and more confidence in what's flowing downstream. For new clients, the new configuration-driven setup makes onboarding faster and less manual. And for the team maintaining it all, separating out file and Athena transformations means the pipeline is finally easier to operate day to day.

This one was a long time coming. It's a meaningful step forward in how reliable and scalable our data platform is, and sets us up well for what's next.

Accolades

Spotlights & shoutouts

NameRoleRecognition
Dan Hebert Lead Data Engineer

Dan Hebert walked into the Unified IT Shark Tank Hackathon Finale on June 1st and walked out a winner. His project, The Glow, a preterm birth risk awareness tool that lets any pregnant woman anonymously check her risk level using basic health information and her zip code, took first place.

The concept is exactly what you'd expect from Dan: technically sharp, genuinely useful, and rooted in the mission that drives all of us. No PHI collected. No fluff. Just a smart, accessible tool that could help women have better conversations with their doctors — and quietly showcase what Lucina Analytics is capable of.

We couldn't be more proud. Well deserved, Dan. 🏆

Get to Know the Team

Ethan Kershner
Data Scientist

Hi all! I have met/worked with many of you, but for those of you who I haven't had the chance to work with yet or who may not know me very well, I thought I'd share some facts about myself:

I live in the Philadelphia area and have most of my life. I like it here because this area offers a wide variety of experiences & because my friends/family live here.

I have a very good dog named Summer.

I studied Neuroscience undergrad with a minor in Philosophy. My studies focused on Psychopharmacology (how pharmacology interacts with the mind), studying how mental illnesses can be better treated by better understanding & addressing their neurological underpinnings. I am fascinated by the human mind/brain - how it works and how it is connected with the rest of the body. My two biggest passions are technology/health & I am really grateful to be working in a field that lets me embrace both at the same time. I am currently about halfway through a Master's of Data Science from UT Austin.

I like to try new things often and have a lot of different hobbies that I pick up/put down when I feel drawn to them. Some of these are language learning, music & learning more about the birds in my neighborhood and trying to make friends with them. I like to read fantasy/sci-fi books and right now I am in the very early phases of my second attempt at writing one.

📊 How do you start with a new dataset?
Explore visually first — let the data speak for itself before cleaning.
